summary: Anthony Tribe works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol and completed his DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, Steven Collins, and Paul Williams. He held posts at Montana and Arizona.
Anthony W. Barber is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1984. He held a post attested at the University of Calgary in 1998.
Antoine Lutz completed a PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University under the supervision of Francisco Varela.

Antoine Meillet was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Paris, the Sorbonne, and EPHE under Darmesteter, Lévi, and de Saussure. He held professorships at EPHE, INALCO, and the Collège de France (1905–1936).

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a linguist, historian, and Iranian specialist. He founded the Société Asiatique, serving as its president, and was a professor of Arabic and Persian at INALCO and of Persian at the Collège de France (1806–1838).
Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier (1741–1795) was an Indologist who studied under Ramchandra and served as a colonel in the East India Company.

Antoine-Léonard Chézy was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Silvestre de Sacy and Langlès. He worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, INALCO, and held the chair of Sanskrit at the Collège de France from 1815 to 1832.

Anton Boller was an Austrian linguist and Indologist. He was a corresponding member of the Austrian Academy of Sciences and served as a lecturer and professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Vienna from 1845.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate from Humboldt University of Berlin around 1828–1831. He lectured there in oriental and modern occidental languages (1849–1852) and held a post at the Royal Danish Library.

Anton Schiefner was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. Educated in law at Saint Petersburg State University and Oriental studies at Humboldt University of Berlin, he was an academician at the Russian Academy of Sciences and taught at Saint Petersburg institutions.
Anton Westermann (1806–1869) was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig from 1825 to 1830 and served as co-director there from 1830 to 1865.

Antonello Palumbo works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. He held a research post at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2004) and taught at SOAS University of London (attested 2005–2010).

Antonino Forte was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at EFEO, Hōbōgirin, the Italian School of East Asian Studies, the Istituto Italiano di Cultura in Kyoto, and was a professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1987–2006).

Antonio T. de Nicolás (1930–2022) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD from Fordham University (~1966–1971) and served as professor of philosophy at Stony Brook University from circa 1968 to 1996.

Antonio Terrone is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, and has served as a scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Anuj Misra works in Indology and history/archaeology. Misra studied under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker, and holds an external researcher position attested at the University of Copenhagen for 2026.

Anukul Chandra Banerjee was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Calcutta under Nalinaksha Dutt and Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, later chairing Pali there and directing the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.
Anuradha Seneviratna was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Ceylon (~1963–1968) and later served there as a professor from circa 1984 to 2004.
Anvita Abbi is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Cornell University from circa 1972 to 1975 and served on an editorial board at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Archibald Edward Gough was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as Anglo-Sanskrit Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Professor of Philosophy at Presidency University, and Principal of Aliah University.
